- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing gradual mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike, model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the forecast horizon, particularly after mid-range peaks.
- Forecast bias is stronger in the first 5–10 days, then stabilizes or slightly underestimates later.
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing downward trends; often misses early signs of price correction.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short-term (1–3 days) and overly pessimistic in the long-term (10+ days).
